subject: Pilot pricing: usage-based vs flat-fee extension
messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia@brightbay.com>

Cc: Tim Clark <tim.clark@brightbay.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot extension + billing ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the smooth onboarding last month — the model has been running well against our routing tests. We have one ask as we approach the scheduled end of the 30-day pilot on May 28: would Redwood be open to a two-week extension and, if so, can we switch the extension to a usage-based structure instead of another flat time-boxed fee?

Quick background: our team is evaluating peak vs off-peak behaviour and we expect a spike next week (logistics batching loads). A usage-based charge with a monthly cap would be ideal — it lets us avoid overcommitting but gives you predictable floor revenue. If necessary we could agree to a soft minimum and then a per-1k-token rate above that.

Also attaching the latest usage export for the pilot so you can see the distribution.

Attachments: pilot_usage_report.csv

Let me know whether you need a PO or if a DocuSign amendment is easier.

Thanks,
Lucia
Director of Data & Automation
BrightBay Logistics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia@brightbay.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension + billing ask

Hi Lucia — really glad the tests are looking good. Thanks for the usage CSV, that helps. We can absolutely do an extension and we have two practical options that typically work well for pilots like yours: 

1) Two-week flat extension (time-boxed) with a 15% pilot discount — simple, predictable invoice, no change to billing flow.

2) Two-week usage-based extension with a hard monthly cap plus a soft minimum. Example: $3,000 soft-minimum + $0.90 per 1k tokens above the soft-min, capped at $7,000 for the extension period. Any unused portion of the soft-min can be converted to Redwood credits applied towards a first-month paid plan if you convert to Dedicated within 60 days.

Operational notes: usage-based extensions require us to set a billing cap in the account and enable token-metering for the extension window. We can route peak traffic to a higher-throughput pool if you expect the spike but that would affect the per-token economics — I included a short pricing model doc that shows throughput tiers.

I've attached a one-page pilot amendment (redwood-pilot-amendment-v1.docx) that encodes both options; if you like option 2 we'll need a signed amendment or a PO that references BB-POC-4761. If you prefer, I can loop in Finance to accept a PO.

Thoughts? If you'd like to jump on a 20-min call to pick the right cap/min values given your CSV I can set that up today.

— Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot extension + billing ask (BrightBay)

Marcus/Ben — forwarding Lucia's ask. Quick internal notes below before I send the amendment: 

- Usage profile in CSV: 75% daytime small requests (short sequences), 25% burst windows with longer sequences. Expect a spike on 5/25.
- Margin check: option 2 (usage with cap) looks acceptable if we set the soft-min at $3k and cap at $7k. That preserves ~40% gross margin if average token price behaves as in our model.
- Upside: offer conversion of unused soft-min to Redwood credits (good for conversion motion). It costs us close to nothing to offer credits but improves the customer's willingness to accept usage pricing.
- Risk: if they route to Dedicated-like throughput during spike, unit cost increases. Suggest we include explicit note that throughput-specific kernels may adjust per-token cost; we can auto-fallback to normal pool if cost exceeds threshold.

If agreed I'll send the doc and propose option 2 with the credit-conversion clause. Ben — can you pre-approve the cap terms? Marcus — please flag if Legal needs different language for the credit conversion.

Thanks,
Mina
